title: Direct 3D-Aware Object Insertion via Decomposed Visual Proxies
claim: Strong 2D and 3D-aware baselines fail to place an object in a user-specified pose; ours achieves precise pose control across varied scenes.
layout: 2 stacked panels: (a) 4-image baseline comparison row, (b) two rows of background plus object to result
description: Panel (a) is a row of photos showing a bookshelf scene. On the left, an Input column holds the reference object (a teal and red book) above the empty shelf background. Three larger result images follow, labeled Nano Banana Pro, Object3DIT and Ours. Nano Banana Pro and Object3DIT put the book in an awkward or wrong pose. Ours shows the red book standing upright between the other books. Panel (b) has two rows in an equation layout: background with a translucent orange target region, plus the object with a red rotation-arrow inset, then a gray arrow to the result. The first row uses a pen and a wire desk organizer. The second row uses a Starry Night painting and a living-room wall, and the result has a red dashed zoom-in box. The eye goes first to the colorful book comparison in the top row.
caption: Pose-controllable object insertion. (a) Existing pipelines have difficulty placing the reference object in a reasonable and user-specified pose within the background image, even when using a strong 2D generative model such as Nano Banana Pro [ref] or a 3D-aware editing model such as Object3DIT [ref]. In contrast, our framework inserts the object with precise pose control and better scene alignment. (b) Additional results show that our method achieves high-fidelity insertion with precise pose control in complex real-world scenes. We report the prompts used for competing methods in Appendix [ref].
abstract: Object insertion aims to seamlessly composite a reference object into a specified region of a background image. Recent diffusion-based methods achieve high visual quality but formulate insertion as a simple 2D inpainting task, providing no explicit control over the object's 3D pose and limiting their practical applicability. We propose DIRECT (Decomposed Injection for Reference Composition and Target-integration), a novel framework that integrates interactive pose manipulation with high-fidelity 2D image synthesis to enable pose-controllable object insertion. Our method decomposes the insertion conditions into three complementary components: appearance guidance capturing visual details from the reference object, geometry guidance derived from the user-adjusted 3D proxy, and context guidance from the target background. By injecting them through separate pathways, DIRECT avoids feature entanglement and simultaneously preserves reference appearance, follows the user-specified pose, and adapts the object to the target scene. We also introduce an automated data construction pipeline to improve the diversity and quality of training data. Experiments show that DIRECT outperforms previous methods in both geometric controllability and visual quality.
